__inputs.name: DS_CLICKHOUSE
__inputs.label: Cloudflare Analytics Engine
__inputs.description: Altinity ClickHouse datasource pointed at the Cloudflare AE SQL API. Setup: mcp-server/src/docs/operations/GRAFANA.md

title: GST MCP Server
description: Analytics Engine dashboard for the GST MCP server. Panels cover only event types that actually emit in production — see the 'What this dashboard deliberately does not show' panel. Every count uses sum(_sample_interval), not count(), because AE samples.

list.name: dataset
list.label: Dataset
list.description: AE dataset. Production carries the traffic; staging is near-empty by design (no cron, little use).

panels.title: Trial signups over time, by outcome
panels.description: Every branch of POST /trial/signup emits one event. A rising 'unavailable' line means a secret is unbound or Upstash/Turnstile is failing — the failure mode that is otherwise invisible without a live wrangler tail. Empty until the trial goes live in production.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t, blob4 AS outcome, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'trial_signup' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob4, t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Signup outcomes in window
panels.description: The signup-health view. 'minted' and 'reissued' are successes; everything else is a refusal or a fault. Compare 'unavailable' against the rest to read the failure rate.

targets.query:
SELECT blob4 AS outcome, blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'trial_signup' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob4, blob6
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Distinct active trials
panels.description: uniq(blob8) over trial tool calls. SAMPLING CAVEAT: uniq has no sample correction — Cloudflare corrects count/sum/avg/quantile only — so this is EXACT while the dataset is unsampled and a LOWER BOUND once it is not, dropping the quietest talkers first. It under-reports, never over-reports. For an exact count of live trials use GET /admin/oauth/m2m-clients and count tier === 'trial'. See ADR-0031.

targets.query:
SELECT uniq(blob8) AS distinct_trials
FROM $dataset
WHERE index1 = 'OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL' AND blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter

panels.title: Per-trial call volume (top talkers)
panels.description: The 'is someone farming this' view. Sample-correct: sum(_sample_interval) is the corrected form of count(). blob8 is the per-client dimension (OAUTH:<clientId>) — a blob, never the index, so index1 stays roster-sized (ADR-0031).

targets.query:
SELECT blob8 AS client, sum(_sample_interval) AS calls
FROM $dataset
WHERE index1 = 'OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL' AND blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob8
ORDER BY calls DESC
LIMIT 50

panels.title: Invocations over time, by primitive
panels.description: Tools, Resources and Prompts. The event-type allowlist is explicit rather than a bare GROUP BY blob1, so this panel cannot silently plot event types the dashboard says it omits.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t, blob1 AS event_type, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('tool_invocation', 'resource_read', 'prompt_invocation') AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob1, t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Invocations over time, by keyOwner
panels.description: index1 is the AE sampling key and is deliberately roster-sized: one value per team key, plus one constant per M2M tier (all trials share OAUTH:M2M:TRIAL). Unauthenticated and cron traffic lands in __none__.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t, index1 AS key_owner, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('tool_invocation', 'resource_read', 'prompt_invocation') AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY index1, t
ORDER BY t

SELECT blob2 AS name, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2
ORDER BY n DESC
LIMIT 25

SELECT blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 IN ('tool_invocation', 'resource_read', 'prompt_invocation') AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob6
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Tool latency percentiles
panels.description: Server-side handler latency, weighted by sample interval. Same query shape the /status page renders (status-metrics.ts), with the dataset and time window macro-swapped. Includes probe/synthetic traffic — it is real handler latency.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS name,
       quantileWeighted(0.5, double1, _sample_interval) AS p50_ms,
       quantileWeighted(0.95, double1, _sample_interval) AS p95_ms,
       quantileWeighted(0.99, double1, _sample_interval) AS p99_ms,
       sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Outcomes by tool
panels.description: success vs error per tool. A tool appearing only with outcome 'error' is the shape worth chasing.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS name, blob4 AS outcome, sum(_sample_interval) AS n
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'tool_invocation' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, blob4
ORDER BY n DESC

panels.title: Zone-1 calls over time, by category
panels.description: blob7 = '1' isolates Zone-1 categories from the OAuth refresh path. This is the Inoreader-funded budget the radar tools draw on, and the reason radar is denied to the trial tier.

targets.query:
SELECT $timeSeries AS t, blob2 AS category, sum(_sample_interval) AS calls
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'inoreader_call' AND blob7 = '1' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, t
ORDER BY t

panels.title: Inoreader calls by category, outcome and status
panels.description: status_code '0' isolates network-side failures from Inoreader-side ones.

targets.query:
SELECT blob2 AS category, blob4 AS outcome, blob6 AS status_code, sum(_sample_interval) AS calls
FROM $dataset
WHERE blob1 = 'inoreader_call' AND $timeFilter
GROUP BY blob2, blob4, blob6
ORDER BY calls DESC

panels.title: What this dashboard deliberately does not show

options.content:
Five of the twelve event types declared in `mcp-server/src/metrics/_schema.ts` **emit nothing in production**. A panel over any of them would render an empty chart that reads as *good news* — "no throttling", "all healthy" — rather than *no data*. So they are absent on purpose, and a guard test (`mcp-server/tests/unit/observability/grafana-dashboard.test.ts`) fails if one is added back.

| Not shown | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Rate-limit pressure** (`rate_limit_decision`) | Declared in the schema with `allow`/`throttle`/`deny` outcomes and **no emitter anywhere**. Throttles reach AE for no tier at all. Tracked as **BL-157**. |
| **Health checks** (`health_check`) | Same: declared, never emitted. `/status` health comes from live probes (`buildHealthPayload`), not from AE. |
| **Prompt spans** (`prompt_span`) | Emitter exists (`metrics/prompt-span.ts`); nothing calls it. |
| **IRL counters** (`wrong_irl_detected`, `gate_elided`) | Emitters exist (`metrics/irl-ingestion-events.ts`); nothing calls them. |
| **Audit batches** (`audit_batch`) | Emitted, but the pipeline is deactivated (ADR-0014), so counters legitimately read 0. |
| **Cron outcomes** (`cron_outcome`) | Genuinely live — omitted because `/status` and the seven alert rules already cover cron health. Add a panel here if that stops being true. |

**Expected empty at import**: the trial panels, until the self-serve trial goes live in production. An empty trial panel is not a broken query.

**Reading the numbers**: every count is `sum(_sample_interval)`, not `count()`, because AE samples. `uniq()` has no such correction — see the caveat on the *Distinct active trials* panel and [ADR-0031](https://github.com/reidperyam/gst-website/blob/master/src/docs/adr/0031-per-client-analytics-identity-is-a-blob.md).
